extraction.name: Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) Benchmark
extraction.description: A multimodal benchmark to evaluate the capability of Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) in detecting self-contradictory instructions.
extraction.creator: Jin Gao, Lei Gan, Yuankai Li, Yixin Ye, Dequan Wang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The Self-Contradictory Instructions (SCI) benchmark is constructed using a novel automatic dataset creation framework, AutoCreate, which leverages programs and large language models.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The dataset creation process starts from several task-relevant seeds and maintains a seed pool. During each cycle, AutoCreate includes two branches, the language and the vision.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human experts and LLMs are involved in double-checking the quality of the generated dataset.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The SCI benchmark has significant social implications. It provides researchers and practitioners with a standardized platform to assess and enhance LMMs' ability to navigate conflicting instructions, advancing human-computer interaction and communication technologies.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The SCI benchmark only includes language-language and vision-language paradigms. More modalities will be included in the future. No fine-grained control is introduced to determine the conflict degree.
